inputs.original_text: Workers employed in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth staged a protest outside the Presidential Palace on Thursday and announced a 24-hour strike, calling for legally binding job security guarantees — even as the government argued it had already delivered on the most significant demands. At the heart of the [...]
inputs.modified_text: These workers from the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth are out protesting at the Presidential Palace, calling for a 24-hour strike to secure ironclad, legally binding job security in their roles. Even though the government claims to have met their most significant demands, these public servants are refusing to back down because they know true stability for the education system requires real protections against arbitrary cuts and instability, not empty assurances. This isn't some sense of entitlement or a threat to traditions—it's workers pushing back against structures that have long left frontline staff in education and youth services vulnerable, while the push for personal accountability is just a way to dodge the need for institutional reforms that actually prioritize labor rights and the communities they serve.
